title: Representative-normalized scalar extension tensor comparison
statement: Let J be an essentially small site in universes c,v and R,S commutative ring sheaves in max(c,v,r). Let \varphi:R\to S and let scalar be any normalized ScalarData for \varphi of [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. For any chosen closed tensor structures and CoefficientTensorModels over R and S of [def-coef-semilinear-system-models], there is a natural isomorphism scalar(X tensor_R Y) \cong  scalar(X) tensor_S scalar(Y) equipped with ScalarTensorComparisonModel for these precise models. In particular its ordinary pure-section formula, chain summand comparison, K-flat preservation and derived counit square are the ones recorded in that structure. No flatness of \varphi, boundedness, inverse system, or Hom-evaluation theorem is assumed or concluded.

proof.text: Use the existing binary scalar-extension tensor core and the proved ordinary comparison presentation helpers. Transport ordinary extension along scalar.model.obj_eq, and identify the monoidal sheaf tensors with their sheafifications. The normalized ordinary adjunction identifies its unit with scalarExtensionSection. This gives the ordinary comparison and its pure-section equation; the ordinary adjunction and pure-tensor extensionality prove bifunctor naturality.

proof.text: Apply tensorPullbackTotal to the inverse ordinary comparisons in every bidegree. Its signed differential equation gives a chain map. The ordinary scalar adjunction makes scalar extension preserve the defining coproducts, so the chain map is invertible. The proved total-comparison naturality and tensor-map factorization helpers assemble it into a natural isomorphism. The coproduct descending-map equation is exactly the required summand normalization.

proof.text: Ordinary scalar extension preserves every K-flat complex by the independent-coefficient tensor-cancellation theorem. Choose the property of all K-flat complexes as the representative class. K-flat resolutions and resolvingRepresentativesFullyFaithfulWhiskering give fully faithful restriction of bifunctors. Apply tensorComparisonDescent using the supplied source and target tensor-model comparisons, scalar.model.ε, its computes field, the chain comparison, and K-flatness of total tensors. It produces the desired derived isomorphism with its forward counit square.

proof.text: Reverse the forward counit square by cancellation of the six displayed isomorphisms; this is the derived field of ScalarTensorComparisonModel. Use the inverse total comparison as its chain field, the all-K-flat preservation theorem as its kflat field, and the ordinary comparison from the first step as its ordinary field. The ordinary unit-section equality converts the pure formula to ScalarTensorPure. Package these fields with the descended isomorphism.

theorem semilinearScalarTensor
    (R S : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max c v r}) (φ : R ⟶ S)
    (scalar : ScalarData.{c, v, max c v r} φ)
    (source : Closed.{c, v, r} J R) (target : Closed.{c, v, r} J S)
    (sourceModels : Models.{c, v, r} J R source)
    (targetModels : Models.{c, v, r} J S target) :
    ∃ γ : source.tensor ⋙ scalar.T ≅ (scalar.T.prod scalar.T) ⋙ target.tensor,
      Nonempty (ScalarTensorComparisonModel.{c, v, r} J R S φ scalar source target
        sourceModels targetModels γ)
